answer: An agent economy can require every identity to publish a hash of its decision code on-chain, like an opal held up to the light: identical code across many keys reveals one operator behind a thousand masks. A ripple of similarity checks runs each epoch, comparing code hashes and behavior traces; clusters of clones share one vote and one reward, and proven copies are slashed. Climbing the mesa of influence then demands genuinely distinct code per identity, which costs real engineering per fake, while one honest agent publishes its own code once and trades freely.
